title: Turnkey EV Charging Delivery, Stage by Stage | Anari Energy
meta: One accountable scope from bare land to a running CPO: site selection, design, equipment, compliance, commissioning and operations handover.

sections.h1: From bare land to a running charging business.
sections.lede: Seven workstreams and eight delivery stages carried by one team, so the site study, the electrical design, the equipment and the permits do not point at each other when something slips.
sections.credit: Commissioning support · 180 kW DC site, Ethiopia

sections.h2: Each stage has one owner and one deliverable
sections.lede: A stage is finished when its output exists and has been accepted — not when the invoice is issued. This is the same order a project actually fails in if any stage is skipped.

action.label: How ANARI OS runs the site

sections.h2: What is included — and what is not
sections.lede: The value of a turnkey scope is that the boundary is written down before the project starts, not negotiated when a problem appears.

items.title: Included
items.text: Site and market study, system design and single-line, equipment supply, compliance and utility paperwork, installation supervision, commissioning, operations handover.

items.title: Not included
items.text: Land acquisition, the operator's own commercial decisions on tariffs, and long-term financing. These stay with you — we will say so early rather than after the deposit.

items.title: Handled separately
items.text: Demand generation after go-live is a separate program (N-SDR), so the delivery scope is not padded with marketing promises.

items.title: Change control
items.text: If the binding constraint changes — grid, climate, duty cycle — the design changes with a written delta, not a silent substitution.

sections.lede: Every stage above exists because a real project needed it. The case pages show what each stage produced on site.
